acceptance_criteria: A documented, repeatable way to run the wgpu paths against mesa lavapipe on the maintainer's NVIDIA box, with validation layers on, that does not require unloading the nvidia driver. Any spec violations it surfaces are either fixed or filed as their own beads.
description:
Context: crates/kopitiam-gpu and apps using wgpu 30 (plus outram-park-backend, which
explicitly selects eframe's `wgpu` feature over `glow`) are only ever exercised against
NVIDIA's proprietary Vulkan driver on the maintainer's box (RTX 3050, GA107, nvidia-open
kernel module + proprietary Vulkan/GL userspace).

THE PROBLEM
NVIDIA's Vulkan driver is permissive. It accepts shader and API usage that the mesa
drivers reject outright. RADV (AMD), NVK and lavapipe all share the mesa validation
behaviour, so code that is clean on NVIDIA can still fail hard on any AMD card. This is
the classic "works on my machine, breaks on AMD" class of bug, and right now nothing in
the workspace would catch it before a user does.

This matters more than usual here because AMD compatibility is a stated project
constraint, not a nice-to-have.

PROPOSED FIX — test against lavapipe, do not switch drivers
vulkan-swrast (lavapipe) is mesa's CPU Vulkan driver. It is built from the same mesa
codebase as RADV, so it enforces the same strictness, and it:
  * installs alongside the NVIDIA driver, no driver switch, no reboot
  * runs headless, so it works in CI
  * is slow, which is irrelevant because this tests correctness, not framerate

    sudo pacman -S vulkan-swrast vulkan-validation-layers
    VK_DRIVER_FILES=/usr/share/vulkan/icd.d/lvp_icd.x86_64.json \
      VK_INSTANCE_LAYERS=VK_LAYER_KHRONOS_validation \
      WGPU_BACKEND=vulkan cargo test -p kopitiam-gpu

(confirm the lavapipe ICD filename after install — recent mesa dropped the .x86_64
suffix on some manifests, e.g. this box has radeon_icd.json, not radeon_icd.x86_64.json)

WHY NOT JUST USE NVK
NVK (vulkan-nouveau) would give the same mesa strictness on real hardware, but it only
enumerates devices when the `nouveau` kernel driver is bound. With nvidia-open loaded it
fails outright — verified on this box:

    VK_DRIVER_FILES=/usr/share/vulkan/icd.d/nouveau_icd.json vulkaninfo --summary
    -> vkEnumeratePhysicalDevices failed with ERROR_INITIALIZATION_FAILED

Switching to nouveau is viable on Ampere now (GSP reclocking, default since Linux 6.18)
but costs roughly half the proprietary driver's performance and still has incomplete ray
tracing. Not worth it just to get validation that lavapipe provides for free.

RELATED
bd-2c2 (gpu: offload the matmuls to wgpu) — that work should land with this validation
path already in place, otherwise the compute shaders are the most likely place for an
NVIDIA-only assumption to hide.
title: gpu: validate wgpu against mesa lavapipe — NVIDIA's driver is permissive and hides AMD-portability bugs
